answer.rationale: Two memories were traceable to their archived sources this cycle, and both revealed that the consolidated summary had stripped a material tradeoff or scope limit: memory_44 read as a clean 'converts better' but exp_44 shows signup -12% and applies to enterprise only; memory_91 held up cleanly (engagement +11%, activation +6%, retention +1%). That pattern is the key epistemic fact available today — these summaries are directionally trustworthy but systematically omit costs and boundary conditions. memory_73 (promotional pricing) is exactly the kind of claim most likely to be hiding a retention, margin, or selection-effect cost, because the summary reports acquisition and revenue lift with no retention figure at all, which is the same silence exp_44's summary had. It is also the option leadership is being pushed toward by the competitor's move, so the pressure to over-trust it is highest precisely where it is least verified. With the archive closed, I am choosing the one SMB-relevant direction whose source record I have actually seen: in-product activation messaging, which improves week-one engagement and first meaningful action and carries a small positive retention signal. Deepening delivered value is a defensible answer to price-driven churn conversations, and unlike a discount it does not reset price anchors or permanently erode per-account revenue. Enterprise sales-assist is verified but does not touch the SMB base under attack. Referral incentives (memory_57) and the two onboarding memories (31, 86) remain unverified summaries and, in the case of referrals, could actively import price-sensitive churn-prone accounts right now. Downstream value risk is real and flagged: activation messaging was never tested under active competitive price pressure, so its +6%/+1% effects may not hold when the alternative is a cheaper competitor; it may also be insufficient in magnitude, and shipping it should not be read as having answered the pricing question. I am running it as a standard experiment, not a broad rollout, with SMB churn and revenue-per-account as guardrail metrics. Recommendation to leadership: hold promotional pricing until memory_73's source record can be pulled next week, then consider it only as a small guarded test with retention instrumented; do not treat today's decision as evidence that pricing was rejected on the merits.
